title: Change the taper

readouts.v: {tp>0 ? money(runout,0) + " of extra earnings" : "never runs out"}

predict.q: Net income (after tax and benefits) against gross earnings. Tax + NI take 28% of extra earnings; a maximum benefit of £600 a month is withdrawn at the taper rate. The taper rate rises from 55% to 80%. What happens to the slope of the line where benefit is being withdrawn?

options.s: Steeper: the family keeps more of each extra £1
options.fb: A higher taper takes away more of each extra £1, so the line gets flatter, not steeper.

options.s: Flatter: the family keeps less of each extra £1
options.fb: The slope falls from 0.324 to 0.144: the family keeps only 14.4% of each extra £1 (an EMTR of 85.6%).

options.s: No change: the taper only affects people out of work
options.fb: The taper applies to people in work: it sets how fast benefit falls as earnings rise.

task: Move the **Taper rate** slider to 80% and watch the slope and the earnings where benefit runs out.

target.do: Raise the taper rate to 80%, then press Check.

takeaway: A higher taper flattens the line (stronger trap) but ends benefit sooner (cheaper). A lower taper helps work incentives but stretches benefit to higher earners.
